definition: PaLM (Pathways Language Model) is a 540 billion-parameter dense decoder-only transformer-based large language model (LLM) developed by Google AI.
details: Researchers also trained smaller versions of PaLM (with 8 and 62 billion parameters) to test the effects of model scale.

explainer.lead: PaLM (Pathways Language Model) is a 540 billion-parameter dense decoder-only transformer-based large language model developed by Google AI. It matters as a demonstration of how model scale affects capability.

tiers.eli5: It is a very large text-prediction model: give it some words and it continues them, and its size is measured in hundreds of billions of adjustable settings.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers treat PaLM as a large dense decoder-only transformer and, for study or constrained settings, work with its smaller 8 and 62 billion-parameter versions. A pitfall is that dense models of this size are expensive to serve.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a dense decoder-only transformer-based large language model with 540 billion parameters; smaller versions with 8 and 62 billion parameters were trained to test the effects of model scale. The reported limits concern scale effects rather than a formal bound.

explainer.example: Researchers compare the 8, 62 and 540 billion-parameter PaLM versions on the same tasks to see how performance changes with scale.
